source.snippet: I'm working on improving the accessibility of a medium-sized website and have identified a number of issues through manual testing and automated accessibility audits... The challenge is that development resources are limited, so fixing everything at once is not reasonable.

problem_statement: Web teams with limited development bandwidth struggle to triage and prioritize WCAG accessibility issues from audit outputs, lacking a structured workflow to decide what to fix first given legal risk, user impact, and dev effort.
target_segment: Web managers, digital accessibility coordinators, and small agency dev teams responsible for WCAG compliance at medium-sized organizations.
notes: WCAG compliance is increasingly legally mandated (ADA, EAA 2025), so buyers have external pressure to spend. Agencies and in-house web teams are paying buyers — accessibility audit tools (axe, Deque) already have commercial tiers. A prioritization layer on top of existing audit output is a gap. Recent post (2026-06-11) with practical workplace context.
